intro: Open one of the five guides for the job in front of you. That can be a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a last check, or clothing on a person. You write your own caption, use a photo of your own goods, and post without a shoot.

Open the guide that matches the job, then open the tool it names. Paste a [product link](page:url-to-video), choose a face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors), or begin from a layout in the [template gallery](page:templates). Downloads do not carry a watermark. [Plans are on the pricing page](page:pricing).

faq.q: Which guide should I open for a product photo or a short ad?
faq.a: It means the opening and the person on screen are already chosen. Your job is the product photo and one sentence you can stand behind, such as the jar holds eight ounces.

faq.q: How do I turn a guide into a file I can post?
faq.a: Pick the guide, then put in a photo of the item you ship. Keep the sentence to something you can show, such as the size on the label. The file you download is the one you post.

faq.q: Why make a short ad instead of waiting on a creator to film?
faq.a: You can change the opening line and export another file without waiting on a creator's calendar. Book the person when the campaign needs that specific face.

faq.q: Who gets the most from these five guides?
faq.a: A person packing orders who also runs the ads will get the most from them. The five pieces are a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a check before you publish, and clothing on a person.

faq.q: Can a beginner make a file from one bottle photo?
faq.a: Yes. If you can photograph the bottle on a table, you can follow the guide. The tool it names is the only app you open for that file.

faq.q: Which products can I make a photo or a short ad for?
faq.a: They point at [beauty](page:ind-beauty-skincare), [fashion](page:ind-fashion-clothing), [food and drinks](page:ind-food-drinks), [home](page:ind-home-living), and [electronics](page:ind-electronics). The same tools work for other goods you ship.

faq.q: Can I start from photos and clips I already shot?
faq.a: Yes. Start with the photo of the item that actually ships, dust and all. A logo file is useful only when you are allowed to put that mark on the ad.

faq.q: Which platforms can I post the photo or the clip to?
faq.a: Use the frame the placement asks for. [Shopify](page:plat-shopify) and [Amazon](page:plat-amazon) want a square photo. A tall 9:16 clip fits [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) and [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts). [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) and [Facebook](page:plat-facebook) can take a square still or a tall clip. Video can also be 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

faq.q: Do I pay before I can open a guide and make a file?
faq.a: Yes. Layouts sit on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Credits pay for each photo or video, and the cost shows before every job.

faq.q: Can I put the downloaded file in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Put the file on a product page or hand it to a client whose brand you are allowed to show. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload.

faq.q: Why start from a guide instead of a blank clothing ad?
faq.a: These guides already decided where the product appears, so your time goes to the claim. A sweater line can say it is merino.

faq.q: How many credits does a product photo or a clip cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A 6-second clip is 24, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Are the faces in the clip real customers?
faq.a: No. The face is generated. Do not give that avatar a customer's name or a line that claims they purchased the product.

steps_h2: How to Turn a Guide Into a Posted Ad
steps_lead: You get a file you can post, and you type the price in the app you already use.

steps.d: Open the guide that matches the job: a product still, a short ad, or a launch clip. You leave with the next file to make.
Upload one clear photo in the tool the guide names. You see the credit cost for the still or the clip before it runs.
Save the file, add the price and caption in the app you already use, then publish it to your store or your ad account.
